standard_prerequisites.name: Lifting formal smoothness along a square-zero ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma labelled lemma-lift-formal-smoothness; invoked at proof lines 45138-45141
standard_prerequisites.use: Performs the induction step, from level n to level n + 1, for the ideal generated by p^n.

core_obligations: Base case: for n = 1 the map is the prime field into the residue field of the Cohen ring, which is formally smooth by the cited characterisation of separable field extensions (proof lines 45134-45136).

Induction step: assuming formal smoothness at level n, apply the lifting lemma to the map Z/p^{n+1} -> Lambda/p^{n+1} Lambda and the ideal I = (p^n), whose square is zero in the source, to obtain formal smoothness at level n + 1 (proof lines 45137-45142).
Conclude by induction on n that the map is formally smooth for every n >= 1 (statement and the two steps above).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of n = 1 through the separable-field-extension criterion (proof lines 45134-45136).
Run the induction using the square-zero lifting lemma for the ideal generated by p^n (proof lines 45137-45142).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a Cohen ring Lambda with residue field of characteristic p the reduction map Z/p^n -> Lambda/p^n Lambda is formally smooth for every n at least one (statement lines 45123-45132). The proof separates the two ingredients: the case n = 1 is formal smoothness of a separable field extension, cited as a characterisation, and the induction step places the ideal generated by p^n, whose square vanishes in the source, so that the cited lifting lemma applies (proof lines 45134-45142). The step that carries the content is the arrangement of the induction, since the lifting lemma needs a square-zero ideal in the source and the author has to note that (p^n) has this property there. Both inputs are same-chapter results, so the card is H2.
